`com.google.javascript.jscomp.DeadAssignmentsElimination.isVariableStillLiveWithinExpression(com.google.javascript.rhino.Node, com.google.javascript.rhino.Node, java.lang.String)`

Why:
- All failures are mis-optimizations of assignments inside expressions with short-circuiting / conditional control flow:
  - `(a = 2) || (a = 3) || a`

  - `(a ? f(b = true) : f(b = false)) && (a = b)`
  - `(f(b = true) || f(b = false)) && (a = b)`
- In each case, the pass removes an assignment too aggressively, replacing `(a = 2)` with `2` or `(b = true)` with `true`, even though the assigned variable may still be read later within the same expression on some reachable evaluation path.

Static evidence:
- `tryRemoveAssignment(...)` only preserves an assignment when:

  - it is live-in and `isVariableStillLiveWithinExpression(...)` returns `true`.
- Therefore, if `isVariableStillLiveWithinExpression(...)` underestimates intra-expression liveness, dead-assignment elimination becomes unsound.

The suspicious code:
- In `isVariableStillLiveWithinExpression(...)`, the `switch` on the parent node type has `case Token.OR`, `case Token.AND`, and `case Token.HOOK`, but there is no specialized handling before falling through into the generic sibling scan.
- The comments say these cases need special conservative handling, but the implementation does not actually do that.
- As a result, the method does not correctly account for reads that occur later in short-circuit / conditional branches, causing assignments in the first operand/branch to be incorrectly removed.

There is also a secondary suspicious helper:
- `com.google.javascript.jscomp.DeadAssignmentsElimination.isVariableReadBeforeKill(com.google.javascript.rhino.Node, java.lang.String)`
